target_customer: Small businesses buying group health insurance, and the payroll platforms that embed it
problem: Small businesses found health insurance quotes and enrollment confusing, slow and broker-dependent, and could not tell if their plan was a good deal.
business_model: Online broker: commissions from carriers on plans sold, plus embedded partnerships with payroll platforms
product_category: Small business health insurance marketplace and administration platform

founders.name: Vivek Shah
prior_employers: Cardpool (YC startup, sold to Blackhawk Network in late 2011)
founders.background_notes: Early employee at Cardpool per the YC launch post; the site lists him as the licensed seller of insurance.

founders.name: George Huo
prior_employers: Cardpool (YC startup, sold to Blackhawk Network in late 2011)
founders.background_notes: Early employee at Cardpool per the YC launch post. A profile site says the founders were MIT-educated engineers (unverified).

competitors.name: Traditional brokers and carrier sites
competitors.what: Offline brokers and direct carrier quoting

technical_complexity.rationale: Quote engine and enrollment forms over carrier data; the hard parts were carrier relationships, licensing and plan data rather than engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Carrier contracts, broker licences and payroll integrations help, but quoting and enrollment are copyable and several better funded rivals emerged.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: By April 2015 TechCrunch named Oscar, Zenefits and Collective Health as competitors; later payroll vendors bundled benefits. SimplyInsured instead became an embedded partner for payroll platforms such as Square Payroll (profile site, unverified).

market_need_then: Affordable Care Act exchanges (SHOP) and 2013-2014 reforms pushed small businesses to re-shop coverage; the launch post cites confusing plans and hidden costs. TechCrunch (2015) reported over $1M monthly sales through carriers including Kaiser and Anthem.

branding.domain_note: Uses simplyinsured.com; acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: Wordmark with Insured set in bold
identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly and reassuring; mission 'eliminate fear in health insurance'

branding.brand_signature: Mission line: eliminate fear in health insurance

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name that says the benefit, but no press on the brand, mascot or community found; crowded with similar insurance names.

pivots.from: Quote engine and plan explainer for individuals and small businesses
pivots.to: Virtual Broker and administrative platform replacing traditional brokers, later embedded via payroll partners
pivots.why: Per TechCrunch the Virtual Broker launched two weeks before April 2015; later partner focus per profile sites (unverified).

outcome_analysis: SimplyInsured launched from YC W13 as a plain-English health insurance quote tool, reached over $1M monthly insurance sales by 2015, and raised a $1.75M seed in April and a $5.9M Series A led by Polaris in June 2015. No later round, acquisition or shutdown was found; the site is live in 2026 under the operating entity Ten 250 Corporation with blog posts last in 2021, which suggests a small surviving business rather than a venture outcome.
notes: A $750K 2013 angel round (YC and Altair) appears on aggregators and FinSMEs snippets but was not opened, so it is unverified and not recorded; total raised differs by source ($7.7M vs $8.42M). The YC page lists only Vivek Shah as founder; the YC launch post names George Huo too. Ownership by Ten 250 Corporation comes from the company site. No dated competitor list exists in the 2013 launch post, so the competitors entry is the incumbent channel only; Oscar, Zenefits and Collective Health are from the 2015 TechCrunch piece and are recorded under takeover_risk.
